1_domain_guard_completeness.independent_enumeration: The kernel has NO validation and NO early return in either engine file. Every conditional in compact_vector_node_view_scope (Accessibility.py:110-163; AccessibilityWElevation.py:106-159, textually identical, loop at 139-157 = the claimed 4-line offset): two unconditional terminal label writes (L131-132/L127-128), two conditional prologue pushes (w_end<cutoff, w_start<cutoff; L137-141/L133-137), seed popped AND discarded (L134-135/L130-131), while-queue (L143/L139), row eligibility c<=cutoff & c<S0[v] (L150-153/L146-149), flag truthy (L159/L155), deg(neighbor)>1 (L160/L156). Numba boundscheck is off, so out-of-domain indices are UB, not exceptions. Public entries raise only where B0 raises: Accessibility.py:594-595 (Centrality) and 649-650 (OD_Matrix) ValueError - both outside the candidate's writable surface. The 12 refusal classes are therefore a NEW admitted-domain filter, not a reproduction of baseline guards, and completeness must be judged as: does any input the guard ADMITS allow candidate behavior to diverge from baseline?
1_domain_guard_completeness.coverage_check: Yes. (a) Classes 1-6 (dtype/ndim of pointer/vector/weights/flags + o_terminal shape/dtype) pin the candidate to exactly the observed specialization (int64/int64/float64/bool, 2-D int64/float64 terminals; matches admission.json's observed_dtypes cross-check and the engine builder's fixed dtypes at Accessibility.py:551-558), preventing silent new specializations with different promotion semantics; the heap key dtype and label dtype both derive from o_terminal_weights, so class 6 is load-bearing and present. (b) Classes 8+9 (pointer[0]==0, nondecreasing, pointer[V]==len(vector); every adjacency_vector[j] in [0,V)) make every kernel array access in-bounds on the admitted route: pointer reads need len>=V+1 (implied by class 1 length>=1 + class 8 consistency), label/adjacency accesses stay in [0,V), and the guard's own reads are in-bounds by construction. (c) Class 10 (finite >=0 weights, signed zero admitted) excludes negative-cycle/NaN domains where baseline behavior is not a sound oracle. (d) Class 11 guards the two unconditional per-origin terminal writes across ALL rows because the guard runs once per driver call on the 2-D driver arrays - per-origin 1-D rows are slices of guarded arrays. (e) Class 12 bounds scratch. (f) 'Not guarded' list verified sound: d_terminal_idxs/d_terminal_weights/d_weights feed ONLY adjust_destination_distances (Accessibility.py:236/304; AWE:232/290) and d_weights ONLY reach_gravity_knn_access (Accessibility.py:311; AWE:297) - both unchanged kernels receiving byte-identical inputs on both routes; o_terminal_weights VALUES enter labels by direct assignment in identical prologue code (no arithmetic). (g) Within admitted classes, value-domain variation (weights values, terminal weight values incl. NaN/inf terminals) flows through identical compare/assign code on both arms - no divergence path. (h) cutoff integer dtype is admitted by class 7; ones(float64)+int promotes identically in the byte-identical prologue; engine passes float search_radius only - noted as PR-N2, no action.
1_domain_guard_completeness.fallback_identity_and_reachability: The original kernel and BOTH drivers' original prange loops remain textually unchanged; the guard only selects a branch inside the driver, so every refusal executes the same compiled functions B0 runs - byte-identical by identity. Reachability and non-engagement are pinned behaviorally (T3 direct int32 kernel call, T4 flt_inf_incidence_weight, T13 per-class refusal with the original path's NRT allocation-rate signature in a bounded child), which is the correct enforcement given the driver's own IR necessarily changes.
1_domain_guard_completeness.divergence_note: PR-N1 (informational, no action): d_count>=0 and d-terminal index ranges are not guarded. Exposure exists only where B0 itself reads/writes out of bounds (boundscheck off), where no byte-oracle exists and both arms are structurally identical UB; the engine builder always produces d_count=len(d_weights)>=0 (Accessibility.py:555). Correctly outside the guarded domain; the A1R reviewer should be aware the byte-oracle does not extend to corrupting inputs.

2_scratch_semantics.verdict: SOUND; D1-D6 within dossier language, confirmed individually
2_scratch_semantics.snapshot_preservation: Phase one reads labels and writes ONLY scratch; phase two reads scratch and writes labels/queue. Every eligibility test therefore sees pre-row S0 - exactly the value L152's gather materializes in B0. Duplicate destinations in one row: both offsets tested against the same S0[v], phase two visits ascending offsets, later (possibly larger) value wins - matches baseline. c values are STORED once and read back in phase two (no recomputation, no second rounding) - matches baseline's read of its computed weights_neighbors[i]. Ascending visit order preserved (scan order = append order = nonzero order). T5 pins this with a first-divergence negative mutant that MUST raise - satisfying the dossier's negative-test requirement for the staging counterexample.
2_scratch_semantics.d1_absolute_offsets: No behavioral effect; phase two needs one load per element, row-local value derivable (off-p0) for journal comparison. Accepted.
2_scratch_semantics.d2_short_circuit: Skips only the pure in-bounds label-gather read when c>cutoff; the skipped read has no side effect and the operand is in-bounds on the admitted route (classes 8/9). Eligible set and stored values identical. Accepted.
2_scratch_semantics.d3_per_origin_allocation: Two buffers allocated INSIDE each prange iteration body - the strongest form of the dossier's ownership clause ('every independent origin/search owns its buffers; no module-global or shared Numba array'). Nothing survives the iteration, so reuse-state independence holds by construction (T11 repetition/permutation, T12 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=4 subprocess pin it). This legitimately supersedes the H05 reasoning's 'per-thread reusable scratch' phrasing - the dossier (authority) requires ownership, not persistence, and the hot path is per-pop.
2_scratch_semantics.d4_max_degree: Computed once per driver call from the unchanged pointer array; with class 8 monotonicity every row length <= max_degree, so phase one can never truncate. Implementation checkpoint PR-N4: with V=0 the max must be defined as 0 (T9 zero-length scratch pins the behavior); the implementer should initialize the max at 0 rather than the first row.
2_scratch_semantics.d5_capacity_bound: Peak live scratch H*max_degree*16 bytes is a sound estimate (workqueue scheduler keeps <= H iterations in flight); 256 MiB cap honors the dossier's 'excessive scratch -> original behavior'. At observed scale (max_degree small) this is a few KB, so the cap only fires on pathological graphs, as intended.
2_scratch_semantics.d6_both_drivers: Both drivers dispatch; original loops retained as fallback. Grep confirms compact_vector_node_view_scope has exactly two callers per engine file (Accessibility.py:225/292; AWE:221/278) - the private route dispatched from both is complete coverage.
2_scratch_semantics.thread_safety_vs_actual_invocation: Verified against the real call pattern: the search kernel is parallel=False (NUMBA_PARALLEL=False at Accessibility.py:47; kernel decorator uses the constant), nogil, called inside each driver's nb.prange over origins. Scratch is iteration-local (no sharing, no atomics needed), labels/queue iteration-local, output cells disjoint per origin, adjacency/terminal arrays read-only on both routes as in B0.
2_scratch_semantics.cleanup_obligation: No early returns or caught errors exist on the private route; any exception unwinds the iteration and NRT frees the per-iteration buffers by refcount - there is no cleanup action that could be gotten wrong, and no state to contaminate future calls. No new exception surface on the admitted domain: the only new writes are scratch[0:n_eligible) with n_eligible <= row length <= max_degree = buffer length (D4), and all other ops are identical to baseline ops on in-bounds operands.

3_compiler_obligation.verdict: CORRECTLY STATED AND ENFORCED BY T1-T17
3_compiler_obligation.byte_equality: Proof section 7.1 demands dtype+shape+bytes equality via comparator.assert_array_bytes_equal with NO tolerance and explicitly rules out the ULP allowance. Verified against the oracle: tests/large_e2e/oracle/comparator.py assert_array_within_ulp docstring states it is used ONLY for pure-Python-trace vs compiled fastmath float sums and that 'Candidate-vs-baseline comparisons NEVER use this - those are assert_array_bytes_equal (bit-exact) without exception.' The proof's statement of availability matches the tooling exactly.
3_compiler_obligation.single_add_no_fma_argument: Sound at the claim level: a single binary float64 add admits no reassociation and has no multiply operand, hence no FMA. Critically, the proof does NOT rest on the source-level argument: section 7.3 makes the IR side-by-side (inspect_llvm, fadd/fcmp, same fastmath set) delivered evidence at A1I/A1R and states 'Any mismatch in semantics between the compiled pair on ANY fixture blocks promotion regardless of the induction' - matching the dossier's blocking rule.
3_compiler_obligation.test_pins: T1/T2 kernel+engine batteries across corpus + new boundary fixtures; T4 includes the NEW true-overflow (sum->+inf, ineligible in both arms via the cutoff compare) and max-float cutoff cases; T5 staged duplicate + negative mutant; T13 refusal routing with allocation-signature non-engagement proof; T14 admitted allocation boundedness (makes the A1 target observable); T15 OD path; T16 observed replay via b0_import.load_arm(UNA_ORACLE_ARM_B=candidate) of replay_integrated_scope_access (2 records) + >=2 OD records byte-exact; T17 no new warnings/exceptions. Negative mutation policy requires the comparator to RAISE and records first divergence. This covers the dossier's proof-required list (induction, compiled equality, IR, mismatch-blocks) item by item.
3_compiler_obligation.flag_freeze: Section 7.4 no-flag-change obligation verified against the source: kernel parallel=NUMBA_PARALLEL=False, drivers hardcode parallel=True (Accessibility.py:202/246; AWE:198/242), cache/nogil/fastmath identical constants - so the new module's stated flag set is the existing one.
